source.stem: What is the correct sequence for blood being pumped from the heart to the lungs?

options.text: left atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary artery
left atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary vein
right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery
right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary vein

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Viruses can multiply outside living cells.

intelligence.enrichment: Microorganisms can be categorised into groups such as protozoa, fungi, bacteria, and some algae. Viruses are microscopic and acellular, and they multiply when they enter a living cell. Observed or stated features -> microbe category or virus boundary -> correct classification. The learner correctly applies this rule: Microorganisms can be categorised into groups such as protozoa, fungi, bacteria, and some algae. Viruses are microscopic and acellular, and they multiply when they enter a living cell. Anything microscopic is basically a bacterium, so the exact category does not matter.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Microorganisms: friend and foe. The student must decide: Decide how to classify examples such as Amoeba, bread mould, bacteria, some algae, and viruses without treating all microscopic things as the same kind of organism. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
